Guidance & outlook: So for full year, we will be doing just 12% - 15% guidance that we have said last time in terms of the volume and on the margin front, 11% - 13%.
Our guidance is 11% to 13% kind of operating margin.
Our guidance for operating margins remains in that 11% to 13%.
Growth & demand: Our volumes for the quarter stood at 40,729 metric tons , degrew by 7% Y -o-Y.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 77 crores, a growth of 93% Y -o-Y, while margins stood at 13%, registering a 600 basis point growth.

Yes, I think the April degrowth of 7% is -- it doesn't keep me up at night because, like you rightly said, fourth quarter, we had delivered a 25% kind of a volume growth, which obviously is not sustainable.
Margins & costs: EBITDA is minus INR 5 crores, and there is no inventory gain for this quarter.

So now there is no inventory gain because what we are seeing the significant improvement in the gross margin for this quarter, close to 30 -odd percent primarily because of the change in inventory, which is kind of INR 100 crores negative figure, and that's why there is a significant improvement.
And at the EBITDA margin, apart from these 2, while volum es degrew, better realizations helped better operating leverage.
Capex & expansion: Despite these external challenges, Prince Pipes remained firmly focused on executing our long- term strategy, which is based on 3 pillars: product innovation, distributor network expansion and retailer network expansion.
For this quarter, around INR 40 crores, INR 42 crores has been spent, and that has primarily been on the completion of second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover.
And what we have guided is 13% to 15% of growth in this year, which translates to, if the capacity is static, then we will reach to around 60% of utilization.
Balance sheet & cash: We expect industry demand to be supported by a recovery in infrastructure activity, increasing premiumization across product categories and the benefits of operating leverage as market conditions normalize.
Receivable days stood at 40 days, whereas inventory days stood at 100 days as of 30th June 2026.
I think the gross debt is around INR 120 crores, kind of, including long-term and short-term both.
Risks & challenges: But I think the good part is that now there is less uncertainty for distributors to be scared of destocking because they are scared of prices to fall further.
So going forward, we will -- we should see good realizations and good growth because of this lack of uncertainty going forward.

But this time, given that the prices were so volatile, we have seen more demand coming in from plumbing and agri has actually seen a major degrowth relative to the rest of the portfolio, which is plumbing and drainage.

guidance.t: And similarly, now because we were looking at 12%, 15% kind of a volume growth, so the ask rate, obviously, in the 9 months is 17% to 21%.
So for full year, we will be doing just 12% - 15% guidance that we have said last time in terms of the volume and on the margin front, 11% - 13%.
I think for now, if I look at medium term, I think 11% to 13% kind of operating margin with industry-leading growth should be the focus.

Guidance & outlook: I think if you have to look at guidance for next financial year -- or current financial year rather, I think EBITDA should be closer to our normal guidance of in the band of 11% to 13% for the full year.
Sir, I want to get a sense, last quarter, I remember the EBITDA margin guidance was 10% to 12%.
I think we are confident of achieving that kind of 11%, 12% kind of EBITDA, including the bathware losses.
Growth & demand: We achieved our highest ever quarterly volumes, delivering a healthy volume growth of 23% Y-o-Y in quarter 4.
For the full year FY '26, our volume growth stood at 8%.
Our volumes for the quarter stood at 62,167 metric tons, a robust growth of 23% Y-o-Y.
Margins & costs: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR110 crores, an exceptional growth of 100% Y -o-Y, while margins stood at 13%, registering a 500 basis point growth.
PAT margins for the quarter stood at 7%, a 400 basis point growth.
EBITDA for the full year stood at INR232 crores, up by 43% Y-o-Y, while margin stood at 9%.
Capex & expansion: So traditionally, South has been a market where we have lagged our peers and a lot of capacity expansion has come in South, but maybe the market share growth has not been in line with the capacity expansion.

And the capex, which you asked about FY '27 plan, it will be in the range of INR200 crores, which includes capex to maintain for our existing plant and some of the debottlenecking plan which we have for our two or three plants.
So 60% was mentioned for the new plant, which we operated for nine months, I'll say, on a full -- on a capacity what we have built in.
Balance sheet & cash: Basic sharp increase in polymer prices during this quarter, the company passed on inventory gains to the distributors and channel partners, thereby fostering distributor relationship and supporting faster inventory movement, which in turn enhanced working capital efficiency and reduced inventory holding costs.
Our working capital efficiency improved significantly in FY '26, driven by sharp reduction in inventory and receivable days.
Receivable days improved to 51 days from 61 days in the same period last year, while inventory days stood at 70 days as of 31st March 2026.
Risks & challenges: FY '26 was a challenging year for the industry, shaped by volatile raw material prices, extended unseasonal rainfall and subdued demand across key end user categories.
Additionally, significant fluctuations in PVC prices disrupted channel sentiment and created added uncertainty across the value chain.
Despite these external headwinds, our focus remains steadfast on strengthening operational resilience while consistently advancing our long-term strategic agenda.

guidance.t: Just a couple of questions from my end, one, you said that you're looking at margins sustaining between 11% to 13%.

And the capex, which you asked about FY '27 plan, it will be in the range of INR200 crores, which includes capex to maintain for our existing plant and some of the debottlenecking plan which we have for our two or three plants.
So we have already guided for 12% to 15% kind of volume growth.
